purpose: Primary Fair Work Commission case ledger preserving dismissal, the five-week transition to alternative employment, a decision not to seek reinstatement, and an ordered compensation remedy without treating the order as payment receipt.

events.geography: Sydney, Australia; Fair Work Commission case [2023] FWC 2632
events.date_precision: dismissal date; decision records alternative employment beginning 2023-06-13 and a compensation order within 21 days
events.denominator: One publicly identified adjudicated worker case; no population denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from the primary Fair Work Commission decision
events.missingness: Payment receipt, alternative-offer set, job duration, household effect, recurrence, collective action, and later trust or exit are not retained
events.exposure: The employer dismissed a qualified mechanic after disputed conduct and performance concerns, without a prior opportunity to respond; the Commission found the dismissal unfair but found a valid underlying reason and reduced the remedy scope accordingly
events.alternatives_before_action: The worker obtained and began alternative employment on 2023-06-13, five weeks after dismissal, earning a little more than in the prior role; the public decision does not enumerate other feasible offers or rejected alternatives
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: The worker had no remuneration during the three weeks the Commission found he would likely have remained employed, and the decision ordered $3,744 gross less tax
events.choice_or_response: The worker challenged the dismissal, sought a separation certificate, obtained alternative employment, and did not seek reinstatement because the new employment and circumstances made return inappropriate
events.person_or_actor_with_control: The employer controlled dismissal and separation documentation; the worker controlled the challenge and job search; the Commission controlled the remedy determination
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: The Commission found the dismissal unfair and ordered $3,744 gross less tax in lieu of reinstatement within 21 days
events.durability_followup: New employment and non-return to the original employer are observed; payment, job duration, recurrence, and household recovery remain unknown
events.immediate_outcome: A five-week transition to alternative employment, a bounded non-return/remedy choice, a defined no-income interval, and an ordered compensation remedy are observed; payment receipt is not
events.protected_outcome: The worker obtained new employment at slightly higher pay and the formal decision supplied a compensation route; longer-term recovery is not measured
events.sacrificed_outcome: The worker lost the original employment and had no income during the assessed three-week notice-period loss; separation-certificate and accrued-leave disputes remained unresolved in the decision
events.cost_risk_transfer: The worker carried search and interim income costs while the employer received a compensation obligation subject to execution
events.later_outcome: New employment and the end of the original employment relationship are observed, but payment receipt, job duration, household recovery, recurrence, later trust, collective action, switching, and exit remain unknown
events.meaning_and_attribution: The record documents a workplace trust dispute and a decision not to seek reinstatement, but does not provide a standardized trust measure or durable identity judgment
events.public_or_collective_response: The worker used the formal Commission route and individual job-search response; no later collective or political action is reported
events.counterexample: Alternative employment can be obtained quickly enough to limit assessed compensation while the worker still loses an employment relationship and faces an interim income gap; an order is not receipt
events.source_and_uncertainty: Primary Fair Work Commission decision [2023] FWC 2632, https://www.fwc.gov.au/documents/decisionssigned/pdf/2023fwc2632.pdf; the decision records dismissal, alternative employment, the five-week gap, no income during the assessed three weeks, and a $3,744 order, but no payment receipt or later follow-up

arrows.evidence: The decision records dismissal on May 9, 2023, no income during the assessed three-week notice-period interval, and a new role beginning June 13, 2023
arrows.counterexample: A new job does not reveal the full offer set, search effort, duration, or equivalence of work
arrows.remaining_gap: Alternative availability, search intensity, job duration, working conditions, and long-term equivalence

arrows.to: non-return and compensation in lieu of reinstatement
arrows.evidence: The worker did not seek reinstatement, the Commission found reinstatement inappropriate in light of alternative employment, and compensation was ordered in lieu of return
arrows.counterexample: A decision not to seek reinstatement is not a standardized trust measure or proof of broad labor-market exit
arrows.remaining_gap: Stated reasons in full, feasible return conditions, later switching, trust, and exit

arrows.from: assessed income gap and alternative employment
arrows.evidence: The Commission assessed three weeks of likely lost remuneration at $3,744, made no deduction for income during that interval, and ordered $3,744 gross less tax within 21 days
arrows.counterexample: An order and deadline do not prove payment receipt, net recovery, or residual loss
arrows.remaining_gap: Payment execution, receipt, taxation, and residual household effect

arrows.to: later recovery, trust, recurrence, or exit
arrows.evidence: The public decision ends at the new role and compensation order without later job, household, trust, recurrence, or exit follow-up
arrows.counterexample: A later job can coexist with unresolved compensation, household strain, or altered trust
arrows.remaining_gap: Payment receipt, job duration, household recovery, later trust, recurrence, action, switching, and exit

arrows.evidence: The decision provides individual compensation but reports no correction to the employer's process, separation-certificate route, or comparable-worker outcome
arrows.counterexample: Individual compensation can coexist with unchanged workplace practices
arrows.remaining_gap: Process correction, recurrence, worker voice, monitoring, and comparable-worker outcomes

boundary: This ledger adds one primary adjudicated case with observed alternative employment, a five-week transition and interim income gap, non-return through compensation in lieu of reinstatement, and an ordered remedy. It does not establish payment receipt, household recovery, durable trust, recurrence, action, switching, or exit.
storage_boundary: No claimant file, direct identifier beyond the public case reference, bulk archive, or payment instrument is retained; only bounded primary decision fields, dates, alternative-employment and remedy stages, uncertainty, and open downstream arrows are represented.

reproduction_audit.result: The official FWC decision remains the case-specific public record located for Westrip; the recheck found no public payment-compliance filing, receipt record, later employment follow-up, household outcome, or exit record tied to U2023/4269.
reproduction_audit.interpretation: This is a public-observation boundary, not evidence that the ordered compensation was unpaid or that no later outcome occurred.
